title: Encryption Boundary Convergence Playbook (v0.1 draft)
body:
Purpose:
This playbook sketches a converged approach for tightening the encryption boundary for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). It focuses on a pragmatic migration path from software KMS and cloud-managed keys to an HSM-backed, auditable envelope-encryption model. The goal is to reduce blast radius for secrets, provide cryptographic attestation for keys, and produce a Terraform-friendly operator pattern for customers running Redwood Private.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane components, secrets backplane, and edge connector services that hold or consume long-term encryption keys.
- Includes: KMS operator changes (on-cluster and external), HSM integration (PKCS#11 and cloud-HSM bridges), Terraform module upgrade notes, audit log capture and retention guidance, and rollback/incident playbooks.
- Out of scope: application-level secret encryption at the developer SDK level (handled in separate docs).

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers may have existing Vault/GCP/AWS KMS-backed secrets stores. Migration must allow gradual cutover.
- On-prem environments have heterogeneous HSM capabilities (some have network HSMs, some rely on vendor PKCS#11 modules).
- Terraform state may be stored remotely (S3-compatible, GCS, etc.) and must be migrated with minimal downtime.
- We must avoid shipping private key material in customer clusters or Redwood control plane.

High-level approach (phased):
1) Inventory and discovery
2) Architectural design + compatibility matrix
3) Terraform module updates and testing harness
4) Staged rollout with canary nodes and telemetry
5) Audit verification + compliance evidence packaging
6) Full cutover + decommissioning of legacy keys

Phase 1 — Inventory and discovery (2–3 weeks)
- Collect current KMS/KV usages (namespaces, services, key IDs): run a secrets inventory tool across clusters and on-prem manifests.
- Output: CSV with columns [cluster, namespace, service, secret_type (enc/kek/data), key_reference, last_rotated, owner].
- Validate which secrets are envelope-encrypted vs stored plaintext.
- Identify HSM presence and connectivity constraints (IP allowlists, shared NICs, gateways).
- Action items:
  - [ ] Run inventory agent: /opt/redwood/bin/secrets-inventory --output inventory-2025-11-xx.csv
  - [ ] Confirm owners for high-risk secrets (PII tokens, signing keys)

Phase 2 — Architecture + compatibility matrix (1–2 weeks)
- Pattern options:
  A) On-cluster KMS operator that proxies to customer HSM (PKCS#11)
  B) External HSM gateway (network service) with TLS-mutual auth + attestation
  C) Hybrid: lightweight on-cluster operator performing envelope encryption with KEK stored in HSM gateway
- Compatibility matrix will list per-customer which options are supported, required firewall rules, and operator resource needs.
- Recommended default for most customers: Pattern C (hybrid) — minimal changes to app stacks, allows rolling key rotation.

Phase 3 — Terraform module updates and notes (iterative)
- Goals for modules:
  - Add an abstracted kms_provider block to existing modules (backwards compatible).
  - Provide provider implementations: software_kms, external_hsm, cloud_hsm (GCP/AWS)
  - Ensure provider-specific inputs are optional and validated with precondition checks.

- Example module API (notes, pseudo-HCL):
  module "secrets-backplane" {
    source = "git::ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//secrets-backplane?ref=v3.2"
    name_prefix = var.name_prefix
    kms_provider = var.kms_provider # "software_kms" | "external_hsm" | "cloud_hsm"
    external_hsm = var.external_hsm # map with {endpoint, ca_bundle, client_cert_secret}
    retention_policy = var.audit_retention_days
  }

- Migration path notes:
  - Provide migration script terraform plan/apply sequence:
    1) Add provider block with new default (no-op) settings to allow plan to succeed.
    2) Create new HSM-wrapped KEK resources (staged names) while leaving old KEKs in place.
    3) Roll encryption of a small set of secrets (canary) to new KEKs using a migration job that re-encrypts values.
    4) Validate canary, then batch re-encrypt for remaining secrets.
    5) Decommission legacy KEKs once all consumers confirm.

- Terraform state considerations:
  - Tag new resources with migration metadata to make rollbacks possible (migration_id, previous_key_id).
  - Keep old keys in state until decommission step; do not purge until at least N retention windows (N=7 days by default).
  - Use remote state locking during migration tasks.

Phase 4 — Rolling rollout / ops playbook (detailed)
- Canary strategy:
  - Pick a low-risk namespace (metrics exporters, non-critical webhooks)
  - Set traffic mirroring for reads when possible to verify decryption under both keys
- Operational steps for each roll unit:
  1) Create KEK in HSM (or create HSM key reference) via operator API.
  2) Update Terraform to reference new KEK id (create resources with migration_id).
  3) Run re-encrypt job: k8s job: reencrypt-secrets --from-key old --to-key new --namespace X
  4) Run integration tests and smoke checks.
  5) Observe audit logs and verify remote attestation events (if HSM supports).
  6) If failure, revert: reencrypt --from-key new --to-key old using preserved old KEK id (do not delete old key).

Phase 5 — Audit logs and evidence (continuous)
- Requirements:
  - All KEK creation/rotation/destruction events must be captured with timestamp, actor, and attestation blob (if available).
  - Secret re-encryption jobs should emit a migration_id and list of secret IDs processed.
  - Capture HSM admin/partition events if exposed by vendor API.
- Recommended logging pipeline:
  - Push operator audit events to a tamper-evident sink (append-only GCS/S3 with Object Lock or WORM storage, or to an on-prem ledger service).
  - Export daily digest to a compliance bucket with retention policy aligned to customer SLA.

Terraform module implementation notes and pitfalls
- Provider version pinning: avoid >= without upper bound for pkcs11 providers; many vendor providers have breaking changes. Recommend: provider_version = "~> 1.4.2"
- PKCS#11 path discovery: do not assume /usr/lib/; allow explicit module_path var and fallback discovery script.
- HSM healthcheck probe: implement a periodic probe (GET /health) that verifies sign/encrypt operations with a short-lived test key and writes metrics to Prometheus.
- Secrets rotation hooks: add a lifecycle hook in the module that triggers a k8s job when a KEK id changes (to automate re-encryption).

Example operational terraform snippet (notes):
- Add the new block, plan, and apply with -target to create HSM keys first:
  terraform apply -target=module.secrets-backplane.hsm_key_resource
- Use precondition checks in modules to prevent accidental destruction of old KEKs:
  precondition {
    condition = var.allow_key_deletion == true || length(var.keep_old_key_ids) > 0
    error_message = "Key deletion blocked: set allow_key_deletion=true to proceed or populate keep_old_key_ids."
  }

Security hardening checklists (quick)
- Network:
  - [ ] HSM gateway only accessible from operator control plane CIDRs.
  - [ ] mTLS enforced on all operator <-> HSM communication.
- Key handling:
  - [ ] No private key material stored unencrypted on disk.
  - [ ] KEK identifiers are canonical and rotatable.
- Access controls:
  - [ ] RBAC policy: only operator service account can call HSM wrap/unwrap endpoints.
  - [ ] Human admin actions gated by approval workflow (gitops PR + approval).
- Observability:
  - [ ] Audit events emitted to append-only store.
  - [ ] Prometheus metrics for success/failure counts of re-encrypt jobs and HSM ops.

Incident response & rollback notes
- If decryption failures spike after a KEK rotation:
  1) Pause new reads from the new KEK (flip a feature flag).
  2) Re-enable reads from old KEK and trigger async backfill to correct records.
  3) Preserve attestation blobs and escalate to vendor support if HSM reports hardware faults.

Open questions / unresolved items (needs engineering R&Es)
- HSM attestation format: standardize on CHIP/TPM attestation vs vendor-specific blobs.
- How to provide customers with verifiable proof-of-rotation without leaking key fingerprints? (We can publish signed rotation manifests referencing key IDs and attestation hashes.)
- Performance impact on latency for small-chat workloads when wrapping/unwrapping per-request vs caching unwrap results per worker.

Testing and validation matrix
- Unit: module-level input validation for new kms_provider values.
- Integration: simulate PKCS#11 using SoftHSM v2 in CI and run end-to-end re-encryption flow.
- Load: measure decode latency at p50/p95 for token-serving flows with KEK wrap/unwrap cached vs no-cache.
- Compliance: produce evidence bundle with key lifecycle events and re-encryption migration logs for auditors.

Quick migration runbook (operator on-call friendly)
- Prechecks: verify remote-state lock, run terraform plan and save plan.out.
- Execute low-risk canary re-encryption (namespace=canary).
- Verify application metrics for 24 hours.
- Progressively increase batch size.
- Finalize by tagging legacy KEKs as deprecated and schedule deletion after retention window.

Appendix: useful commands and pointers
- SoftHSM quickstart (for CI): apt-get install softhsm2; softhsm2-util --init-token --slot 0 --label test --so-pin 1234 --pin 1234
- Re-encrypt job example: kubectl create job reencrypt-canary --image=ghcr.io/redwood/reencrypt:canary -- reencrypt --from-key=${OLD} --to-key=${NEW} --namespace=canary
- Audit export: gsutil cp -r gs://redwood-append-only/audit-2025-11-* /tmp/audit-checks/

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive in module behavior while leaving vendor-specific HSM integration details to follow-up PRs.
- We should coordinate with Solutions Eng before publishing a customer-facing migration guide; their playbooks and firewall templates need to align with the final operator behavior.

TODOs:
- [ ] Spike: implement SoftHSM in CI and run the re-encrypt workflow (owner: Marco, due: 2025-11-20)
- [ ] Draft HCL examples for every provider type (owner: Sana, due: 2025-11-28)
- [ ] Create telemetry dashboard template (owner: Jeremy, due: 2025-12-05)

End of draft.
